# Loading Packages and Data
Opening the homework dataset from the HW2 Folder. 
Creating a Seurat Object from the data and looking at meta.data. 

```{r load new packages, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

if (!require("here")) {install.packages("here"); require("here")}
if (!require("Seurat")) {install.packages("Seurat"); require("Seurat")}

Dataset <- Read10X(data.dir = here("rt_code", "HW2", "Dataset"))

shotgun_kidney <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = Dataset, project = "Kidney_snRNA", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200 )
shotgun_kidney[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(shotgun_kidney, pattern = "^mt-")
head(shotgun_kidney@meta.data)

here()

```

# Purpose and Background
<span style="color:#956f13">This is the second homework assignment using snRNAseq analysis with 5 questions. This document serves to expand the scope of the understanding of cells beyond the glomerulus by analyzing a shotgun kidney dataset with all of the cells of the kidney. The meta.data includes DNA barcodes, features, and a matrix. The barcodes assist to assign an identity to each specific cell, the features are seen as the individual genes, and the matrix cross references the information and tells gene expression across the cells.  </span> 

# Question 1
Analyze the shotgun kidney snRNAseq dataset.     
a) What filtering parameters did you choose? Why?    
<span style="color:#956f13">I chose to put the feature count at greater than 200 and less than 3000. This would allow for removal of low quality cells with low gene expression. Additionally, the the upper bound at 3000 was a little conservative, but it allowed for a filter of possible doublets in the dataset. Lastly, I made limit for the the mitochondrial percentage of cells 15% in order to retrieve intact cells to be best of my ability.  </span>  

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Creating a violin plot before setting parameters for the data
VlnPlot(shotgun_kidney, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
before <- ncol(shotgun_kidney)

#Applying parameters to the dataset and making another violin plot to compare it to the original 
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- subset(shotgun_kidney, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 3000 & percent.mt < 15)
after <- ncol(filtered_shotgun_kidney) 
VlnPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
```

b) How many cells do they filter out?      
<span style="color:#956f13">The parameters filtered out 956 cells.  </span>  

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Making a table to display the amount of cells being filtered with parameters applied to the snRNAseq dataset. 
cell_counts <- data.frame(Phase = c("Before Filtering", "After Filtering", "Amount Filtered" ), Cell_Number = c(before, after, before-after))
print(cell_counts)
```


# Question 2 {#question2}
What resolution did you decide to use to maximize clustering diversity?  
<span style="color:#956f13">I used 0.08 for my resolution.  </span>

```{r setup-analysis, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.show='hide', results='hide'}
# Normalize and Scale the data
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- NormalizeData(filtered_shotgun_kidney, normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 10000)
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- FindVariableFeatures(filtered_shotgun_kidney, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

# Label what the top 10 genes are 
top10 <- head(VariableFeatures(filtered_shotgun_kidney), 10)

# Plot the variable genes in the dataset, and label the top 10
plot1 <- VariableFeaturePlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney)
plot2 <- LabelPoints(plot = plot1, points = top10, repel = TRUE)
plot2
all.genes <- rownames(filtered_shotgun_kidney)

# Rescale the data and run a PCA that prints the top 5 genes for each of the first 5 PCs
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- ScaleData(filtered_shotgun_kidney, features = all.genes)
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- RunPCA(filtered_shotgun_kidney, features = VariableFeatures(object = filtered_shotgun_kidney))
print(filtered_shotgun_kidney[["pca"]], dims = 1:5, nfeatures = 5)

# Create plots for the genes driving the PC to analyze the clustering of cells 
VizDimLoadings(filtered_shotgun_kidney, dims = 1:2, reduction = "pca")
DimPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, reduction = "pca")
ElbowPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney)

# Set parameters to be able to make a UMAP plot to analyze clusters 
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- FindNeighbors(filtered_shotgun_kidney, dims = 1:10)
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- FindClusters(filtered_shotgun_kidney, resolution = 0.08)
filtered_shotgun_kidney <- RunUMAP(filtered_shotgun_kidney, dims = 1:10)
```


```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Synthesize a umap to look at the clusters with the applied resolution
DimPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, reduction = "umap")
```

a) How many clusters did you get?   
<span style="color:#956f13">I got 12 clusters.  </span>

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
#Find the top 5 genes in each cluster, and group them by cluster 
Shotgun.markers <- FindAllMarkers(filtered_shotgun_kidney, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25)
Shotgun.markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>% top_n(n = 5, wt = avg_log2FC)

top5 <- Shotgun.markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>% top_n(5, avg_log2FC)

#Give the graph a title as all of the clusters are labeled by number
Idents(filtered_shotgun_kidney) <- filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data$seurat_clusters
DimPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, label = T) + ggtitle("Unidentified Cell Clusters in the Kidney")
```

b) Name the clusters at two different levels of specificity.  

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Apply names to the clusters based on a more specific level of specificity 
filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data <- filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data %>% mutate(subclass.rpt = dplyr::case_when(
seurat_clusters == 0 ~ "PTS2",
seurat_clusters == 1 ~ "PTS1",
seurat_clusters == 2 ~ "Endo",
seurat_clusters == 3 ~ "TAL",
seurat_clusters == 4 ~ "PC",
seurat_clusters == 5 ~ "PTS3",
seurat_clusters == 6 ~ "DCT",
seurat_clusters == 7 ~ "dTL",
seurat_clusters == 8 ~ "Perivascular",
seurat_clusters == 9 ~ "IC-B",
seurat_clusters == 10 ~ "PT",
seurat_clusters == 11 ~ "Podo"
))

#Rename the graph now with the cell clusters identified 
Idents(filtered_shotgun_kidney) <- filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data$subclass.rpt
DimPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, reduction = "umap", group.by = "subclass.rpt", label = TRUE, label.size = 5) +
  ggtitle("Named Cell Clusters in the Kidney - High Level Specificty")
```

```{r,echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Change the specificty of the cells to a lower level and make another UMAP
filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data <- filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data %>%
  mutate(broadtype = dplyr::case_when(
    subclass.rpt %in% c("PTS1", "PTS2", "PTS3", "PT") ~ "Proximal Tubule",
    subclass.rpt %in% c("TAL", "dTL") ~ "Loop of Henle ",
    subclass.rpt == "DCT" ~ "Distal Tubule",
    subclass.rpt %in% c("PC", "IC-B") ~ "Collecting Duct",
    subclass.rpt %in% c("Endo", "Perivascular") ~ "Vascular",
    subclass.rpt == "Podo" ~ "Podocytes"
  ))

DimPlot(filtered_shotgun_kidney, group.by = "broadtype", label = TRUE, label.size = 5) +
  ggtitle("Named Cell Clusters in the Kidney - Low Level Specificity") 
```

# Question 3
Re-level the clusters in a biological order that makes sense.

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Re-level the clusters in order 
filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data$broadtype <- factor(
  filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data$broadtype,
  levels = c("Podocytes", "Proximal Tubule", "Loop of Henle", "Distal Tubule", "Collecting Duct", "Vascular")
)
print(levels(filtered_shotgun_kidney@meta.data$broadtype))
```

a) How did you decide on the order?  
<span style="color:#956f13">I decided that order from the movement of filtrate throughout the neuron and how it travels from the glomerular capillaries to the collecting duct, but the vascular component is last because of its indirect support with oxygen and blood.</span>


# Question 4
Identify and print the DEGs that define one of the cell types in your dataset.   
```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Finding the differentially expressed genes for podocytes while cross-referencing it against IC-B cells
cluster0.markers <- FindMarkers(filtered_shotgun_kidney, ident.1 = "Podo", ident.2 = "IC-B", min.pct = 0.25)
podo_specific_genes <- cluster0.markers %>% filter(avg_log2FC > 1, pct.1 > 0.7, pct.2 < 0.3, p_val_adj < 0.05)
print(podo_specific_genes)
```
